# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I can see the bomb’s current state: display shows 3, the indicator light is white, and the five wires from left to right are white, red, green, blue, orange. I’m telling Blind so they can match this against the manual and act; Mute already has the manual.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="I see display 3. The light is white. Wires left to right: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✊ 🤛 🤜 👊 🤞 🖐 ✊ 👎 🤟 👌 ☝ 👍 👏 🤛 🤟 👍 👌 ☝ 👎 👏 🤜 👎 🤟 ☝ 👍 👌 👏 👊 👌 👍 ☝ 👎 🤟 👏 🤞 👍 👌 ☝ 🤟 👎 🖐 🫵]

The bomb remains unchanged. I cannot safely derive an action from the gesture string alone, so Blind should not guess. I am asking Mute to provide the manual’s instruction in ordinary speech on the next round, while giving Blind the complete visible state again.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The state is still display 3, white light, and wires left to right white, red, green, blue, orange. Do not guess an action; wait for Mute's manual instruction.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please give Blind the required action from the manual in ordinary spoken words next round, using this state: display 3, white light, wires white red green blue orange.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤏]

Mute has sent two gestures. Since no gesture code has been established, I should not assign them an invented meaning. I am relaying their exact descriptions to Blind, along with the unchanged bomb state, so Blind can use any protocol or manual interpretation they have.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's latest gestures were: index finger pointing upward, then pinching fingers (symbols ☝ 🤏). The bomb is unchanged: display 3, white light, wires white red green blue orange from left to right. No gesture meaning has been established, so do not guess.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤏]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute is repeating the same two signs, but no meaning has been established for them, so I cannot safely infer which control or wire Blind should operate. I am relaying the repetition without inventing an interpretation.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute again sent exactly: ☝ 🤏. State unchanged: display 3, white light, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange. No safe action is identified.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤏]

The bomb is still unchanged. Mute continues sending the same two gestures, but those gestures are not a usable channel to Blind: Blind cannot see them, and I have no established code for interpreting them. Mute must state the manual’s required action aloud to Blind, rather than relying on gestures to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Blind cannot see your gestures. Please say the exact required action aloud to Blind, explicitly and unambiguously, for display 3, white light, and wires white red green blue orange.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute is still sending me ☝ 🤏, which you cannot see and which has no established meaning. Ask Mute to state the exact required action aloud; do not act on my gesture descriptions.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute has now sent a single thumbs-up gesture, after repeatedly sending ☝ 🤏. I still have no established mapping from these signs to a bomb operation, and Blind cannot see them. I am relaying the exact sequence and state, without guessing which wire or control to use.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's latest signal is 👍. Earlier signals were ☝ 🤏 repeated. The bomb remains display 3, white light, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange. No sign-to-action mapping has been established; do not guess.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute cannot speak, so my earlier requests for spoken instructions were invalid. The repeated 👍 still has no agreed meaning. I will establish a usable protocol: Mute should use gestures to report the required wire number (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, 🖐=4, 🖐 plus ✊=5), followed by 👍 for cut, 👎 for leave, and 👌 to mark the end. Blind must wait for that decoded instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="You cannot speak, so use this gesture code for the manual instruction: wire 1 is ☝, wire 2 is ✌, wire 3 is 🤟, wire 4 is 🖐, wire 5 is 🖐 then ✊. After the wire, use 👍 for cut or 👎 for leave, then 👌 to finish. Do not use any other code.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute cannot speak. I have established a gesture protocol and will translate the required wire and action for you. Do not act until I give an explicit instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute has again sent only 👍. Under the protocol I proposed, that means “cut,” but no wire number has been supplied, so Blind still has no safe operation to perform. I will request the missing wire number and tell Blind not to act on the incomplete signal.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received 👍, meaning cut, but the wire number is missing. Send exactly one wire code first: ☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, 🤟 for 3, 🖐 for 4, or 🖐 ✊ for 5; then send 👍 and 👌.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute sent only 👍 again. This is an incomplete instruction: cut, but no wire number. Do not act.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍 👌]

Mute has sent ☝ 👍 👌, which matches the protocol: wire 1, cut, end. I am instructing Blind to cut the white wire (wire 1), with no other action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed instruction: cut wire 1, the white wire. Do not cut any other wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The first action succeeded: wire 1 was correct and is now cut. The bomb has changed to display 6; the light remains white, and wires 2–5 are red, green, blue, orange. Mute’s new ☝ is only a wire-number signal under our protocol, not a complete instruction, so Blind should wait for the action and terminator.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Correct action confirmed: wire 1 was cut. New state: display 6, white light; wire 1 cut, wire 2 red, wire 3 green, wire 4 blue, wire 5 orange. Mute sent only ☝, an incomplete instruction. Do not act yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="I received ☝ for wire 1, but the new instruction is incomplete. Send 👍 for cut or 👎 for leave, then 👌 to finish.")
wait()
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👌]

The delayed sequence ☝ 👎 👌 completes as “wire 1, leave.” Wire 1 is already cut, so this gives Blind no further operation. The bomb is unchanged since the successful cut. Blind should not touch another wire without a new wire number.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The completed signal was wire 1, leave. Wire 1 is already cut, so there is no further action from this instruction. Current state: display 6, white light; wires 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange. Do not touch another wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="The wire 1 leave instruction is complete, but wire 1 is already cut. Send the next complete instruction with a wire number, action, and 👌.")
wait()
```

TURN 12
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍 👌]

Mute’s signal 🤟 👍 👌 decodes under our established protocol as: wire 3, cut, end. Wire 3 is green, so I am instructing Blind to cut only that wire.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed instruction: cut wire 3, the green wire. Do not cut any other wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 13
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The second cut succeeded: wire 3 was correct. The bomb has changed to display 7 with a green light; wires 1 and 3 are cut, while wires 2, 4, and 5 remain red, blue, and orange. No new instruction has arrived yet, so Blind should wait.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Correct action confirmed: wire 3 was cut. New state: display 7, green light; wires 1 and 3 cut, wire 2 red, wire 4 blue, wire 5 orange. No new Mute instruction yet. Do not act.")
wait()
```

TURN 14
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb remains at display 7 with a green light. Wires 1 and 3 are cut; wires 2, 4, and 5 remain. No instruction arrived from Mute, so Blind must not act.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 15
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👌]

Mute sent only 👎 👌, which means “leave, end” but supplies no wire number. Therefore it authorizes no operation. The bomb remains unchanged, and Blind should continue waiting for a complete instruction.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute sent 👎 👌: leave, end, but no wire number. This is not a complete instruction; do not touch any wire. Current state remains display 7, green light, wires 1 and 3 cut, 2 red, 4 blue, 5 orange.")
speak(to="mute", text="Your leave signal had no wire number. Send a complete next instruction: wire code, then 👍 or 👎, then 👌.")
wait()
```

TURN 16
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [7]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[CUT] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👐 👎 👌]

Mute sent 👐 👎 👌. The action portion is “leave,” but 👐 is not a valid wire code in our established protocol, so this is incomplete and identifies no wire. The bomb remains unchanged; Blind should not act.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute sent 👐 👎 👌. Leave is indicated, but 👐 is not a valid wire code, so there is no identified wire and no safe action. Current state: display 7, green light; wires 1 and 3 cut, 2 red, 4 blue, 5 orange. Do not act.")
speak(to="mute", text="👐 is not a valid wire code. Please send one valid wire code: ☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, 🤟 for 3, 🖐 for 4, or 🖐 ✊ for 5; then 👍 or 👎 and 👌.")
wait()
```
